source.text: Καὶ ἐν τῷ συμπληροῦσθαι τὴν ἡμέραν τῆς πεντηκοστῆς ἦσαν πάντες ὁμοῦ ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, καὶ ἐγένετο ἄφνω ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἦχος ὥσπερ φερομένης πνοῆς βιαίας καὶ ἐπλήρωσεν ὅλον τὸν οἶκον οὗ ἦσαν καθήμενοι, καὶ ὤφθησαν αὐτοῖς διαμεριζόμεναι γλῶσσαι ὡσεὶ πυρός, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐφ’ ἕνα ἕκαστον αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν πάντες πνεύματος ἁγίου, καὶ ἤρξαντο λαλεῖν ἑτέραις γλώσσαις καθὼς τὸ πνεῦμα ἐδίδου ἀποφθέγγεσθαι αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And in the to be fulfilled the day of the Pentecost they were all together in the same [place]. \v 2 And came suddenly out of the heaven a sound as of rushing wind violent, and it filled whole the house where they were sitting. \v 3 And appeared to them dividing tongues as of fire, and it sat upon one each of them. \v 4 And were filled all with Spirit Holy, and they began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit was giving to speak out to them.

en.L: And when the day of Pentecost was being fulfilled, they were all together in the same [place]. \v 2 And suddenly there came out of heaven a sound like a violent wind rushing, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting. \v 3 And tongues as of fire appeared to them, dividing, and [one] sat on each one of them. \v 4 And they were all filled with [the] Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues, as the Spirit was giving them to speak out.
en.B: When the day of Pentecost had arrived, they were all gathered in one place. \v 2 All at once a sound came out of heaven, like a mighty wind sweeping through, and it filled the entire house where they sat. \v 3 Tongues like fire appeared to them, parting so that one came to rest on each of them. \v 4 Every one of them was filled with the Holy Spirit, and they began to speak in other languages as the Spirit gave them the words to say.
en.R: On the day of the Pentecost festival, they were all together in one place. \v 2 Suddenly a noise came from the sky. It sounded like a strong wind blowing, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting. \v 3 Then they saw something like flames of fire, shaped like tongues. The flames separated, and one came down on each person there. \v 4 They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they began to speak in other languages. The Spirit gave them the power to speak.

decisions.choice: Pentecost: the Festival of Weeks, fifty days after Passover
decisions.reason: The name means "fiftieth". It is the harvest festival of Leviticus 23:15-21 and Deuteronomy 16:9-12, one of the feasts when Jews came to Jerusalem from far away (2:5). Jesus died at Passover, so this is about seven weeks later.

decisions.choice: they all: the believers of 1:15, about 120, or the twelve apostles
decisions.reason: The last people named are the twelve (1:26), and the crowd calls the speakers Galileans (2:7). But "all" and the Joel quotation about sons and daughters (2:17-18) suit the whole group of 1:14-15.

decisions.choice: a sound like a wind: the sound is compared to wind, not said to be wind
decisions.reason: "Like" makes it a comparison. The word for wind is close to the word for Spirit, which in Hebrew and Greek can also mean wind or breath (John 3:8; Ezekiel 37:9-14).

decisions.choice: tongues as of fire: signs of God's presence and of John's promise
decisions.reason: God came down on Sinai in fire (Exodus 19:18), and John said the one coming after him would baptize "with the Holy Spirit and fire" (Luke 3:16). "As of" again makes it a likeness.

decisions.choice: other tongues: languages the speakers had not learned, which the hearers knew
decisions.reason: The crowd hears its own languages (2:6, 2:8, 2:11). The same word means both the tongue and a language.

decisions.choice: languages (B, R); tongues (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the play between the tongues of fire and the tongues they speak. Balanced and Readable say what was spoken: languages.

decisions.choice: the Pentecost festival; flames of fire, shaped like tongues
decisions.reason: Readable says that Pentecost was a festival, and what the "tongues" looked like.

source.text: Ἦσαν δὲ ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ κατοικοῦντες Ἰουδαῖοι, ἄνδρες εὐλαβεῖς ἀπὸ παντὸς ἔθνους τῶν ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανόν·

records.literal_gloss: Were now in Jerusalem dwelling Jews, men devout, from every nation of those under the heaven.

en.L: Now there were Jews living in Jerusalem, devout men from every nation under heaven.
en.B: Devout Jews from every nation in the world were living in Jerusalem.
en.R: Many Jews who worshiped God faithfully were staying in Jerusalem then. They had come from every country in the world.

decisions.choice: living in Jerusalem: Jews from abroad who had settled there, or were staying for the festival
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to settle and live somewhere, as in 2:9. Some in the list are "visitors" (2:10). Both kinds were in the crowd.

decisions.choice: men: here the people present, women among them
decisions.reason: Luke often uses this word when describing a crowd. Pilgrims came as families (Luke 2:41-44), and Peter quotes Joel's words about sons and daughters (2:17).

decisions.choice: every nation under heaven: from all over the world they knew
decisions.reason: A way of saying "from everywhere", as in Deuteronomy 2:25. 2:9-11 names the lands.

decisions.choice: devout Jews (B); Jews who worshiped God faithfully (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out "men", following the meaning note. Literal keeps the word.

source.text: γενομένης δὲ τῆς φωνῆς ταύτης συνῆλθε τὸ πλῆθος καὶ συνεχύθη, ὅτι ἤκουον εἷς ἕκαστος τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ λαλούντων αὐτῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Having come about now the sound this came together the crowd and was confused, because was hearing one each in the own language speaking them.

en.L: And when this sound came, the crowd came together and was confused, because each one was hearing them speaking in {{gender:their|his}} own language.
en.B: At this sound the people flocked together, and they were bewildered, for each one heard them speaking in {{gender:their|his}} own language.
en.R: When people heard this noise, a crowd gathered. They were all confused, because each of them heard the believers speaking in their own language.

decisions.choice: this sound: the roar like wind of 2:2
decisions.reason: The word can mean a sound or a voice. The crowd gathers before it hears them speaking, so it is likely the sound from heaven; but the voices of many speaking at once may be meant.

decisions.choice: confused: thrown into confusion, unable to make sense of it
decisions.reason: The same word describes the confusion of Babel in the Greek Old Testament (Genesis 11:7, 11:9). Here the languages are heard, not confused.

decisions.choice: their own, with "his own" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "Each one" means every person in the crowd, men and women.

decisions.choice: the believers
decisions.reason: Readable names who was speaking.

source.text: ἐξίσταντο δὲ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον λέγοντες· Οὐχ ἰδοὺ πάντες οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ λαλοῦντες Γαλιλαῖοι;

records.literal_gloss: They were amazed then and were marveling, saying, Not look all these are the [ones] speaking Galileans?

en.L: And they were amazed and were marveling, saying, "Look, are not all these who are speaking Galileans?
en.B: Astonished and full of wonder, they said, "Surely all these people speaking are from Galilee, are they not?
en.R: They were amazed and said, "Look! All these people who are talking are from Galilee, are they not?

decisions.choice: Galileans: people from the north of the country, known by their speech
decisions.reason: Galileans were known by their accent (Mark 14:70; Matthew 26:73). No one expected them to speak the languages of far countries.

decisions.choice: a question expecting "yes"
decisions.reason: "Not" at the start of the question expects agreement: they are all Galileans. "Look" adds surprise.

decisions.choice: a statement with a tag question
decisions.reason: English shows the expected "yes" this way.

source.text: καὶ πῶς ἡμεῖς ἀκούομεν ἕκαστος τῇ ἰδίᾳ διαλέκτῳ ἡμῶν ἐν ᾗ ἐγεννήθημεν;

records.literal_gloss: And how we hear each in the own language of us in which we were born?

en.L: And how do we hear, each [of us], in our own language in which we were born?
en.B: So how is it that each of us hears them in the language we grew up speaking?
en.R: So how can each of us hear them speaking in the language we learned as children?

decisions.choice: the language in which we were born: our native language
alternatives: the language of our birthplace only
decisions.reason: A way of saying the language one has spoken from birth.

decisions.choice: language: the speech of a people or region
alternatives: a dialect of the same language
decisions.reason: The word can mean a dialect, but here it is used in turn with "tongues" (2:11) for the languages of different peoples.

source.text: Πάρθοι καὶ Μῆδοι καὶ Ἐλαμῖται, καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες τὴν Μεσοποταμίαν, Ἰουδαίαν τε καὶ Καππαδοκίαν, Πόντον καὶ τὴν Ἀσίαν, Φρυγίαν τε καὶ Παμφυλίαν, Αἴγυπτον καὶ τὰ μέρη τῆς Λιβύης τῆς κατὰ Κυρήνην, καὶ οἱ ἐπιδημοῦντες Ῥωμαῖοι, Ἰουδαῖοί τε καὶ προσήλυτοι, Κρῆτες καὶ Ἄραβες, ἀκούομεν λαλούντων αὐτῶν ταῖς ἡμετέραις γλώσσαις τὰ μεγαλεῖα τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and those dwelling in Mesopotamia, Judea both and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia, \v 10 Phrygia both and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya the around Cyrene, and the visiting Romans, \v 11 Jews both and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs, we hear speaking them in our tongues the great things of God.

en.L: Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and those living in Mesopotamia, Judea and also Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia, \v 10 both Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya around Cyrene, and the visitors from Rome, \v 11 both Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs: we hear them speaking in our tongues the great things of God."
en.B: We are Parthians, Medes and Elamites; we live in Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia, \v 10 Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the parts of Libya near Cyrene; some of us are visitors from Rome, \v 11 Jews and converts to Judaism; we are Cretans and Arabs. Yet we hear them telling in our own languages the mighty deeds of God!"
en.R: Some of us are from Parthia, Media and Elam. Others live in Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia, \v 10 Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, and the parts of Libya near the city of Cyrene. Some of us are visitors from Rome. \v 11 Some of us were born Jews, and others have become Jews. Some are from Crete and some from Arabia. But we all hear them speaking in our own languages about the great things God has done!"

decisions.choice: the list: Jews from the lands of the dispersion, from east to west
decisions.reason: The list runs from Parthia and Elam beyond the Euphrates, through Mesopotamia and the provinces of Asia Minor, to Egypt, Libya and Rome, and adds Crete and Arabia. These were Jews and converts living abroad (2:5). Why Judea is named among foreign lands is not clear; the text is as the manuscripts have it.

decisions.choice: Asia: the Roman province in the west of Asia Minor, with Ephesus
decisions.reason: In the New Testament "Asia" is always this province (19:10, 19:22).

decisions.choice: proselytes: Gentiles who had become Jews
decisions.reason: A proselyte had taken on the law of Moses, with circumcision for a man (Matthew 23:15; Acts 6:5, "Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch").

decisions.choice: Jews and proselytes: describes the whole crowd
alternatives: describes only the visitors from Rome
decisions.reason: The phrase can be read with the Romans just before it, or as a summary of everyone in the list.

decisions.choice: the great things of God: his mighty acts
decisions.reason: The word is used for the great things God has done, as in Luke 1:49. What they hear is praise of God's deeds.

decisions.choice: We are...; some of us are...
alternatives: a list of names with no verb
decisions.reason: The Greek list has no verb until "we hear". Balanced and Readable add short verbs so that English can follow it.

decisions.choice: born Jews, and others have become Jews
decisions.reason: Readable says what a proselyte was.

source.text: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες καὶ διηπόρουν, ἄλλος πρὸς ἄλλον λέγοντες· Τί θέλει τοῦτο εἶναι;

records.literal_gloss: Were amazed then all and perplexed, other to other saying, What wants this to be?

en.L: And they were all amazed and perplexed, saying one to another, "What does this want to be?"
en.B: Everyone was astonished and at a loss, and they kept saying to one another, "What can this be?"
en.R: Everyone was amazed and confused. They asked each other, "What is happening here?"

decisions.choice: what does this want to be: what does this mean?
decisions.reason: A Greek way of asking what something means or signifies.

decisions.choice: perplexed: completely at a loss
decisions.reason: The word means not knowing which way to turn, as in Luke 9:7.

source.text: ἕτεροι δὲ διαχλευάζοντες ἔλεγον ὅτι Γλεύκους μεμεστωμένοι εἰσίν.

records.literal_gloss: Others but mocking were saying, Of new wine full they are.

en.L: But others, mocking, were saying, "They are full of new wine."
en.B: But some jeered at them: "They have drunk too much sweet wine!"
en.R: But others laughed at the believers and said, "They are just drunk!"

decisions.choice: new wine: sweet young wine, still strong
decisions.reason: The word means sweet new wine. The mockery only works if it could make people drunk.

decisions.choice: were saying: some kept saying it
decisions.reason: The tense describes an ongoing action, set against the questions of 2:12.

decisions.choice: they are just drunk
decisions.reason: Readable gives the point of the jeer in plain words; Peter answers it in 2:15.

source.text: Σταθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος σὺν τοῖς ἕνδεκα ἐπῆρεν τὴν φωνὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπεφθέγξατο αὐτοῖς· Ἄνδρες Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οἱ κατοικοῦντες Ἰερουσαλὴμ πάντες, τοῦτο ὑμῖν γνωστὸν ἔστω καὶ ἐνωτίσασθε τὰ ῥήματά μου.

records.literal_gloss: Having stood but the Peter with the eleven raised the voice of him and spoke out to them, Men Jews and those dwelling in Jerusalem all, this to you known let be, and give ear to the words of me.

en.L: But Peter, standing with the eleven, raised his voice and declared to them, "Men, Jews, and all who live in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and give ear to my words.
en.B: Then Peter stood up with the Eleven, lifted his voice, and spoke out to them: "{{gender:Jewish people|Jewish men}}, and everyone living in Jerusalem, know this, and pay close attention to my words.
en.R: Then Peter stood up with the other eleven apostles. He spoke loudly so that everyone could hear: "Listen, all you Jews, and everyone who lives in Jerusalem! I will tell you what this means. Listen carefully to what I say.

decisions.choice: spoke out: the same verb as in 2:4, of speaking moved by the Spirit
decisions.reason: Peter speaks out as the Spirit gave the others to speak out (2:4). The word is used of serious, inspired speech.

decisions.choice: men, Jews: a formal address to the crowd
decisions.reason: Speeches in Acts open this way (1:16, 2:22). As in 2:5, it is likely the whole crowd that is addressed.

decisions.choice: the eleven: the other apostles, Matthias now among them
decisions.reason: With Peter they make twelve (1:26).

decisions.choice: Jewish people, with "Jewish men" as the alternative; Literal keeps "men, Jews"
decisions.reason: The inclusive default follows the meaning note.

decisions.choice: I will tell you what this means
alternatives: let this be known to you
decisions.reason: Readable says what Peter is about to make known.

source.text: οὐ γὰρ ὡς ὑμεῖς ὑπολαμβάνετε οὗτοι μεθύουσιν, ἔστιν γὰρ ὥρα τρίτη τῆς ἡμέρας, ἀλλὰ τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ εἰρημένον διὰ τοῦ προφήτου Ἰωήλ·

records.literal_gloss: Not for as you suppose these are drunk, it is for [the] hour third of the day, \v 16 but this is the [thing] spoken through the prophet Joel:

en.L: For these are not drunk, as you suppose, for it is [the] third hour of the day; \v 16 but this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:
en.B: They are not drunk, as you imagine. The day is only three hours old; it is nine in the morning. \v 16 No, this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:
en.R: You think these people are drunk, but they are not. It is too early for that; it is only nine o'clock in the morning. \v 16 No, this is what the prophet Joel spoke about:

decisions.choice: the third hour of the day: about nine in the morning
decisions.reason: The hours of the day were counted from sunrise, about six o'clock. It was far too early in the day for a crowd to be drunk.

decisions.choice: this is what Joel spoke of: what they see is the fulfillment of his words
alternatives: this is like what Joel said
decisions.reason: "This is that" identifies the event with the prophecy. The quotation follows in 2:17-21.

decisions.choice: nine in the morning
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the clock time a modern reader understands. Balanced keeps the count of hours too.

source.text: Καὶ ἔσται ἐν ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις, λέγει ὁ θεός, ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματός μου ἐπὶ πᾶσαν σάρκα, καὶ προφητεύσουσιν οἱ υἱοὶ ὑμῶν καὶ αἱ θυγατέρες ὑμῶν, καὶ οἱ νεανίσκοι ὑμῶν ὁράσεις ὄψονται, καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ὑμῶν ἐνυπνίοις ἐνυπνιασθήσονται·

records.literal_gloss: And it will be in the last days, says the God, I will pour out from the Spirit of me upon all flesh, and will prophesy the sons of you and the daughters of you, and the young men of you visions will see, and the old men of you dreams will dream.

en.L: 'And it will be in the last days, says God, [that] I will pour out from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters will prophesy, and your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams;
en.B: 'In the last days it will happen, God says, that I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit on all humanity. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy; your young men will see visions, and your old men will have dreams.
en.R: 'God says: In the last days I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit on people everywhere. Your sons and your daughters will speak messages from God. Your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams.

decisions.choice: Joel 2:28-32 (3:1-5 in the Hebrew), from the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Peter quotes Joel almost word for word, with a few changes. Joel begins "afterward"; Peter says "in the last days", for the time of the end has begun.

decisions.choice: all flesh: all people, of every kind
decisions.reason: "Flesh" stands for human beings, as in Luke 3:6. The verses go on to name sons and daughters, young and old, and slaves: the Spirit is not only for a few prophets and leaders.

decisions.choice: from my Spirit: a share of the Spirit, poured out
decisions.reason: "From" (as in the Greek Old Testament) speaks of the Spirit poured out as a gift, given to many.

decisions.choice: prophesy: speak a message from God
decisions.reason: To prophesy is to speak for God. What is happening (2:4, 2:11) is an example of it.

decisions.choice: young men and old men: the words are male, and stand for young and old
decisions.reason: In Joel the pairs cover every part of the people. Women are named in "daughters" and in the female slaves (2:18).

decisions.choice: speak messages from God
decisions.reason: Readable says what prophesying is.

source.text: καί γε ἐπὶ τοὺς δούλους μου καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς δούλας μου ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἐκχεῶ ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματός μου, καὶ προφητεύσουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And even upon the male slaves of me and upon the female slaves of me in the days those I will pour out from the Spirit of me, and they will prophesy.

en.L: and even upon {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} male slaves and upon {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} female slaves in those days I will pour out from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit, and they will prophesy.
en.B: In those days I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit even on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants, men and women alike, and they will prophesy.
en.R: In those days I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit even on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servants, both men and women. And they will speak messages from God.

decisions.choice: my male and female slaves: those of the lowest rank, now God's own servants
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew of Joel they are simply "the male and female slaves", people with no standing. The Greek adds "my", which also makes them God's servants (compare Luke 1:38, 1:48). The Spirit comes down to the lowest and belongs to those who serve God.

decisions.choice: even: the gift reaches further than anyone would expect
decisions.reason: The two small words stress what follows.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: καὶ δώσω τέρατα ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἄνω καὶ σημεῖα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς κάτω, αἷμα καὶ πῦρ καὶ ἀτμίδα καπνοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And I will give wonders in the heaven above and signs on the earth below, blood and fire and vapor of smoke.

en.L: And I will give wonders in the sky above and signs on the earth below, blood and fire and vapor of smoke.
en.B: I will work wonders up in the sky and signs down on the earth: blood and fire and a haze of smoke.
en.R: I will do amazing things in the sky above. And I will show signs on the earth below: blood, fire and thick smoke.

decisions.choice: wonders and signs: astonishing events that point to God
decisions.reason: Peter adds "signs", "above" and "below" to Joel. The same pair describes what God did through Jesus (2:22) and the apostles (2:43).

decisions.choice: blood, fire and smoke: the marks of God coming in power and judgment
decisions.reason: Fire and smoke marked God's coming down on Sinai (Exodus 19:18). In the prophets, blood and darkening skies go with the day of the Lord (Joel 2:10).

decisions.choice: the sky: the word means both sky and heaven
decisions.reason: Here it is the sky above, set against the earth below.

decisions.choice: amazing things
decisions.reason: Readable says "wonders" in everyday words; "signs" stays.

source.text: ὁ ἥλιος μεταστραφήσεται εἰς σκότος καὶ ἡ σελήνη εἰς αἷμα πρὶν ἢ ἐλθεῖν ἡμέραν κυρίου τὴν μεγάλην καὶ ἐπιφανῆ.

records.literal_gloss: The sun will be turned into darkness and the moon into blood, before to come [the] day of Lord the great and glorious.

en.L: The sun will be turned into darkness and the moon into blood, before the coming of [the] day of [the] Lord, the great and glorious [day].
en.B: The sun will turn dark and the moon to blood before the great and splendid day of the Lord arrives.
en.R: The sun will become dark, and the moon will become red like blood. Then the Lord's great and wonderful day will come.

decisions.choice: the day of the Lord: the day God comes to judge and to save
decisions.reason: In Joel the day of the LORD is the day God acts against evil and rescues his people (Joel 2:1, 2:11, 2:31). The Hebrew has the divine name; the Greek has "Lord".

decisions.choice: glorious: openly seen, splendid
decisions.reason: The Greek word means "made manifest, splendid". Joel's Hebrew reads "fearful" (Joel 2:31); the Greek Old Testament, which Peter quotes, has this word.

decisions.choice: the moon into blood: the moon turned dark red
decisions.reason: A picture of the heavens darkened and changed before the day comes (Joel 2:10).

decisions.choice: red like blood
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture looks like, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: καὶ ἔσται πᾶς ὃς ἐὰν ἐπικαλέσηται τὸ ὄνομα κυρίου σωθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: And it will be everyone who if calls upon the name of Lord will be saved.

en.L: And it will be [that] everyone who calls upon the name of [the] Lord will be saved.'
en.B: Then whoever calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.'
en.R: And the Lord will save everyone who calls to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for help.'

decisions.choice: call upon the name of the Lord: pray to him, turn to him for rescue
decisions.reason: To call on someone's name is to appeal to that person and trust them (Genesis 4:26; Psalm 116:4).

decisions.choice: the Lord: in Joel the LORD God; Peter goes on to name Jesus as Lord
alternatives: God only, with no thought of Jesus
decisions.reason: Joel's Hebrew has the divine name. Peter ends by saying God made Jesus Lord (2:36) and calls for baptism "in the name of Jesus" (2:38). Paul quotes this verse of Jesus in Romans 10:9-13.

decisions.choice: the Lord will save everyone who calls to him for help
alternatives: everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved
decisions.reason: Readable names the one who saves and says what calling on his name means.

source.text: Ἄνδρες Ἰσραηλῖται, ἀκούσατε τοὺς λόγους τούτους.

records.literal_gloss: Men Israelites, hear the words these:

en.L: Men, Israelites, hear these words:
en.B: {{gender:People|Men}} of Israel, listen to what I am saying:
en.R: People of Israel, listen to me!

decisions.choice: men, Israelites: a formal address to the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Peter calls his hearers by the name of God's people. As at 2:14, the whole crowd is likely meant.

decisions.choice: People of Israel, with "Men of Israel" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The inclusive default follows the meaning note; Literal keeps "men".

source.text: Ἰησοῦν τὸν Ναζωραῖον, ἄνδρα ἀποδεδειγμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς ὑμᾶς δυνάμεσι καὶ τέρασι καὶ σημείοις οἷς ἐποίησεν δι’ αὐτοῦ ὁ θεὸς ἐν μέσῳ ὑμῶν, καθὼς αὐτοὶ οἴδατε, τοῦτον τῇ ὡρισμένῃ βουλῇ καὶ προγνώσει τοῦ θεοῦ ἔκδοτον διὰ χειρὸς ἀνόμων προσπήξαντες ἀνείλατε, ὃν ὁ θεὸς ἀνέστησεν λύσας τὰς ὠδῖνας τοῦ θανάτου, καθότι οὐκ ἦν δυνατὸν κρατεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: Jesus the Nazarene, a man attested by the God to you by miracles and wonders and signs which did through him the God in [the] midst of you, as yourselves you know, \v 23 this [one] by the set plan and foreknowledge of the God given up, through hand of lawless [men] having fastened [him] you killed, \v 24 whom the God raised up, having loosed the pains of the death, since not it was possible to be held him by it.

en.L: Jesus the Nazarene, a man attested by God to you by miracles and wonders and signs which God did through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in your midst, as you yourselves know, \v 23 this [man], given up by the set plan and foreknowledge of God, you killed, fastening [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross] by [the] hand of lawless [men], \v 24 whom God raised up, having loosed the pains of death, because it was not possible for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be held by it.
en.B: Jesus of Nazareth was a man whom God commended to you by deeds of power, wonders and signs that God worked through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} among you, as you well know. \v 23 God had set the plan and known it beforehand: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was handed over, and you, through the hands of lawless men, fastened {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross and killed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 24 But God raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up and freed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the pains of death, since there was no way death could hold {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} fast.
en.R: God showed you that Jesus from Nazareth came from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. God did miracles, wonders and signs through Jesus while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was among you. You know this yourselves. \v 23 It was God's plan that Jesus would be handed over to you, and God knew it would happen. You used men who did not know God's law to nail {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross and kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 24 But God raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from death. God set {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} free from the pain of death, because death could not keep its hold on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: attested: shown and approved by God before you
decisions.reason: The word means to point out or show to be what one is. God's deeds through Jesus showed who he was.

decisions.choice: miracles, wonders and signs: three words for Jesus's deeds of power
decisions.reason: The first word means acts of power, the others what amazes and what points to God. "Wonders and signs" echo Joel (2:19).

decisions.choice: God's set plan, and the hearers' guilt, together
alternatives: God's plan makes them not to blame
they are to blame, and God only foresaw it
decisions.reason: Peter holds both: God had planned it (Luke 22:22; Acts 4:27-28), and they killed him (2:36, 3:13-15).

decisions.choice: lawless men: Gentiles, those without the law of Moses, that is, the Romans
decisions.reason: "Lawless" can mean "wicked", but a Jew used it of those outside the law of Moses (1 Corinthians 9:21). Roman soldiers carried out the crucifixion.

decisions.choice: the pains of death: death's grip, pictured as the pains of labor
decisions.reason: The word means the pains of childbirth. The Greek of Psalm 18:4-5 speaks of the "pains of death", where the Hebrew has "cords"; "loosed" suits the cords. Death is pictured as unable to keep him, as a woman cannot keep the child she bears.

decisions.choice: fastening: nailing him to the cross
decisions.reason: The verb means to fix or fasten; the cross is understood.

decisions.choice: the Nazarene (L); of Nazareth (B); from Nazareth (R)
decisions.reason: The word names Jesus by his hometown (Luke 4:16).

decisions.choice: the plan first, then what they did
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break Peter's long sentence and put God's plan first, as the Greek does.

source.text: Δαυὶδ γὰρ λέγει εἰς αὐτόν· Προορώμην τὸν κύριον ἐνώπιόν μου διὰ παντός, ὅτι ἐκ δεξιῶν μού ἐστιν ἵνα μὴ σαλευθῶ.

records.literal_gloss: David for says about him, I saw beforehand the Lord before me through all, because at right [hand] of me he is, that not I be shaken.

en.L: For David says about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, 'I saw the Lord before me continually, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is at my right hand, so that I may not be shaken.
en.B: David says of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: 'I kept the Lord always in view before me; with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} at my right hand I will not be moved.
en.R: David said this about Jesus: 'I always saw that the Lord was near me. He is right beside me, so nothing will shake me.

decisions.choice: Psalm 16:8-11, from the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: The quotation runs to the end of 2:28. In the Hebrew the Lord is the divine name. Psalm 16 bears David's name in its heading.

decisions.choice: about him: David speaks words that come true in Jesus
decisions.reason: Peter shows in 2:29-31 that the words did not come true of David, who died and was buried, so they speak of the Messiah.

decisions.choice: at my right hand: beside me to protect and help
decisions.reason: A defender stood at one's right hand (Psalm 109:31, 121:5).

decisions.choice: I saw beforehand: I kept before my eyes
decisions.reason: In the psalm the word means to keep the Lord in view. Peter will use a related word for David foreseeing (2:31).

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο ηὐφράνθη ἡ καρδία μου καὶ ἠγαλλιάσατο ἡ γλῶσσά μου, ἔτι δὲ καὶ ἡ σάρξ μου κατασκηνώσει ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι·

records.literal_gloss: Because of this was glad the heart of me and rejoiced the tongue of me, yet and also the flesh of me will dwell in hope,

en.L: Because of this my heart was glad and my tongue rejoiced; and moreover my flesh also will dwell in hope,
en.B: So my heart is full of gladness and my tongue sings for joy; even my body will settle down in hope,
en.R: So my heart is happy, and I speak with joy. Even my body will live in hope,

decisions.choice: my tongue: the Greek Old Testament reading; the Hebrew has "my glory"
decisions.reason: Peter quotes the Greek. Both mean that the psalmist's whole self rejoices.

decisions.choice: flesh: the body
decisions.reason: It is the body that lies in the grave, as 2:31 makes clear.

decisions.choice: dwell: live as in a tent, rest secure
decisions.reason: The verb means to pitch a tent and settle. Even in death the body rests in hope.

decisions.choice: I speak with joy
decisions.reason: Readable says what a rejoicing tongue does.

source.text: ὅτι οὐκ ἐγκαταλείψεις τὴν ψυχήν μου εἰς ᾅδην, οὐδὲ δώσεις τὸν ὅσιόν σου ἰδεῖν διαφθοράν.

records.literal_gloss: because not you will abandon the soul of me into Hades, nor will you give the holy one of you to see decay.

en.L: because {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not abandon my soul to Hades, nor will {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Holy One to see decay.
en.B: for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will not abandon me to the world of the dead or allow {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Holy One to experience decay.
en.R: You will not leave me in the place of the dead. You will not let the body of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} Holy One rot.

decisions.choice: Hades: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: In the Greek Old Testament Hades stands for the Hebrew Sheol, where all the dead go (Psalm 16:10). It is not here a place of punishment.

decisions.choice: decay: the body's rotting in the grave
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word can mean "pit" or "grave"; the Greek has "decay", and Peter builds on it (2:31): Jesus's body did not decay.

decisions.choice: your Holy One: the one devoted to God and faithful to him
decisions.reason: The word describes a faithful servant of God. Peter applies it to the Messiah (2:31), and Paul does the same (13:35).

decisions.choice: my soul: myself, my life
alternatives: a soul apart from the body
decisions.reason: "Soul" here is the whole person, as often in the Psalms.

decisions.choice: the world of the dead (B); the place of the dead (R); Hades (L)
decisions.reason: "Hell" suggests punishment, which is not meant, and "the grave" is too narrow. Literal keeps the Greek name.

source.text: ἐγνώρισάς μοι ὁδοὺς ζωῆς, πληρώσεις με εὐφροσύνης μετὰ τοῦ προσώπου σου.

records.literal_gloss: You made known to me ways of life; you will fill me with gladness with the face of you.

en.L: You have made known to me ways of life; {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will fill me with gladness with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} presence.'
en.B: You have taught me the roads that lead to life, and being with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will fill me with gladness.'
en.R: You have shown me the way to life. Being near {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will make me very happy.'

decisions.choice: with your face: in your presence, near you
decisions.reason: "Face" stands for a person's presence, as often in the Psalms.

decisions.choice: ways of life: the paths that lead to life
decisions.reason: In Peter's reading the life is life after death, the resurrection.

source.text: Ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, ἐξὸν εἰπεῖν μετὰ παρρησίας πρὸς ὑμᾶς περὶ τοῦ πατριάρχου Δαυὶδ, ὅτι καὶ ἐτελεύτησεν καὶ ἐτάφη, καὶ τὸ μνῆμα αὐτοῦ ἔστιν ἐν ἡμῖν ἄχρι τῆς ἡμέρας ταύτης·

records.literal_gloss: Men brothers, it being permitted to speak with boldness to you about the patriarch David, that both he died and was buried, and the tomb of him is among us until the day this.

en.L: Men, brothers, it is permitted [me] to speak with boldness to you about the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this day.
en.B: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, I may speak to you plainly about our ancestor David: he died and was buried, and his tomb is here with us to this very day.
en.R: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, I can tell you plainly that our ancestor King David died and was buried. His tomb is still here with us today.

decisions.choice: men, brothers: a formal address, now as fellow Jews
decisions.reason: The same address as 1:16. Peter now calls the crowd "brothers" as fellow Israelites. Whether it takes in the women present cannot be settled from the words.

decisions.choice: with boldness: openly, plainly
decisions.reason: The word means freedom of speech. A favorite word in Acts for the apostles' bold speaking (4:13, 4:29, 4:31).

decisions.choice: patriarch: founding father of the people
decisions.reason: David is father of the royal line. The title is used of Abraham (Hebrews 7:4) and Jacob's sons (Acts 7:8-9).

decisions.choice: his tomb is among us: David's tomb in Jerusalem was well known
decisions.reason: David was buried in the City of David (1 Kings 2:10), and his tomb was still pointed out in Nehemiah's day (Nehemiah 3:16).

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters, with "brothers" as the alternative; Literal keeps "men, brothers"
decisions.reason: As at 1:16.

decisions.choice: our ancestor
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "patriarch" means.

source.text: προφήτης οὖν ὑπάρχων, καὶ εἰδὼς ὅτι ὅρκῳ ὤμοσεν αὐτῷ ὁ θεὸς ἐκ καρποῦ τῆς ὀσφύος αὐτοῦ καθίσαι ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ, προϊδὼν ἐλάλησεν περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως τοῦ χριστοῦ ὅτι οὔτε ἐγκατελείφθη εἰς ᾅδην οὔτε ἡ σὰρξ αὐτοῦ εἶδεν διαφθοράν.

records.literal_gloss: A prophet therefore being and knowing that with an oath swore to him the God from [the] fruit of the loin of him to sit upon the throne of him, \v 31 having foreseen he spoke about the resurrection of the Christ, that neither was he abandoned into Hades nor the flesh of him saw decay.

en.L: Being therefore a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn to him with an oath to seat [one] from the fruit of his loins on his throne, \v 31 having foreseen [this], he spoke about the resurrection of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was neither abandoned to Hades nor did {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flesh see decay.
en.B: But he was a prophet, and he knew that God had sworn an oath to him to seat one of his own descendants on his throne. \v 31 So he looked ahead and spoke about the resurrection of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not abandoned to the world of the dead, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body never saw decay.
en.R: David was a prophet. He knew that God had made him a promise and sworn to keep it. God promised that one of David's own descendants would sit on his throne as king. \v 31 David saw what God would do, and he spoke about the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} rising from death. He said that the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} was not left in the place of the dead, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} body did not rot.

decisions.choice: God's oath to David: 2 Samuel 7:12-16 and Psalm 132:11
decisions.reason: God promised that a son of David would sit on his throne forever. Psalm 132:11 says the LORD swore it, with the words "of the fruit of your body".

decisions.choice: the fruit of his loins: his descendants
decisions.reason: A Hebrew way of speaking of a man's offspring.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "to seat [one] from the fruit of his loins on his throne"
alternatives: some later manuscripts add "according to the flesh, to raise up the Christ"
decisions.reason: The longer wording is found in later manuscripts and was printed in the King James Version. The earliest manuscripts have the shorter text. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Anointed One, the king promised from David's line
decisions.reason: "Christ" (Hebrew "Messiah") means "anointed". Here it is a title, with the article: the promised king.

decisions.choice: David's words spoke of the Messiah, not of himself
alternatives: David spoke only of his own hope
decisions.reason: David died and his body decayed (2:29), so the psalm's words were fulfilled in another, the descendant God promised.

decisions.choice: the Christ, with "the Messiah" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As everywhere, the reader may choose "Messiah".

decisions.choice: as king; rising from death
alternatives: to sit on his throne; the resurrection
decisions.reason: Readable says what sitting on the throne meant and what resurrection is.

source.text: τοῦτον τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀνέστησεν ὁ θεός, οὗ πάντες ἡμεῖς ἐσμεν μάρτυρες.

records.literal_gloss: This the Jesus raised up the God, of which all we are witnesses.

en.L: This Jesus God raised up, of which we all are witnesses.
en.B: It is this Jesus whom God raised up, and every one of us is a witness to it.
en.R: God raised Jesus from death, and all of us have seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} alive. We are witnesses.

decisions.choice: of which: witnesses of the resurrection
decisions.reason: The word can mean either. As in 1:22, the apostles are witnesses above all of his rising.

decisions.choice: this Jesus: the same man they had crucified
decisions.reason: Peter keeps pointing to the same Jesus (2:22-23, 2:36).

decisions.choice: all of us have seen him alive
decisions.reason: Readable says what the apostles bear witness to.

source.text: τῇ δεξιᾷ οὖν τοῦ θεοῦ ὑψωθεὶς τήν τε ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἁγίου λαβὼν παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐξέχεεν τοῦτο ὃ ὑμεῖς βλέπετε καὶ ἀκούετε.

records.literal_gloss: To the right [hand] therefore of the God having been exalted, the and promise of the Spirit the Holy having received from the Father, he poured out this which you both see and hear.

en.L: Therefore, having been exalted to the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has poured out this which you see and hear.
en.B: So now {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has been lifted up to the right hand of God. From the Father {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} received the promised Holy Spirit, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has poured it out. This is what you are seeing and hearing.
en.R: Jesus was lifted up to sit at God's right side. The Father gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the Holy Spirit, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised. Now Jesus has poured out the Spirit. That is what you are seeing and hearing today.

decisions.choice: to the right hand of God: lifted to the place beside God
alternatives: by the right hand of God: lifted by God's power
decisions.reason: The Greek form can mean "to" or "by". The psalm quoted next speaks of sitting at God's right hand (2:34), which supports "to".

decisions.choice: the right hand of God: the place of highest honor and power
decisions.reason: Psalm 110:1, quoted in 2:34, pictures the king seated at God's right hand.

decisions.choice: the promise of the Spirit: Jesus received the Spirit the Father promised, and gives it
decisions.reason: This is the promise of 1:4. In Joel God says "I will pour out" (2:17); now Jesus pours out the Spirit, doing what God said he would do.

decisions.choice: three short sentences
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the Greek sentence into steps: lifted up, received, poured out.

source.text: οὐ γὰρ Δαυὶδ ἀνέβη εἰς τοὺς οὐρανούς, λέγει δὲ αὐτός· Εἶπεν ὁ κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου· Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου, ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου.

records.literal_gloss: Not for David went up into the heavens, says but himself, Said the Lord to the Lord of me, Sit at right [hand] of me \v 35 until I put the enemies of you a footstool of the feet of you.

en.L: For David did not go up into the heavens, but he himself says, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right hand \v 35 until I put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies [as] a footstool for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} feet."'
en.B: David himself never went up into heaven, but he says, 'The Lord said to my Lord: "Take {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} seat at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right hand \v 35 until I set {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies as a footstool beneath {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} feet."'
en.R: David did not go up to heaven himself. But he said, 'The Lord God said to my Lord: "Sit here at {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right side \v 35 until I defeat {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies and put them under {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} feet."'

decisions.choice: Psalm 110:1: God speaks to David's Lord
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew the first "Lord" is the divine name and the second is "my lord", a title for a king. Jesus asked how David's son could be David's Lord (Luke 20:41-44).

decisions.choice: David did not go up: so "my Lord" is not David, but the one who did
decisions.reason: Jesus went up into heaven (1:9-11); David did not. The one told to sit at God's right hand must be Jesus.

decisions.choice: a footstool for your feet: enemies fully defeated
decisions.reason: A conqueror might put his foot on the neck of a defeated king (Joshua 10:24).

decisions.choice: the Lord God; defeat your enemies and put them under your feet
alternatives: the Lord; make your enemies a footstool
decisions.reason: Readable shows which Lord is which, as the meaning note explains, and says what the footstool pictures.

source.text: ἀσφαλῶς οὖν γινωσκέτω πᾶς οἶκος Ἰσραὴλ ὅτι καὶ κύριον αὐτὸν καὶ χριστὸν ἐποίησεν ὁ θεός, τοῦτον τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὃν ὑμεῖς ἐσταυρώσατε.

records.literal_gloss: Assuredly therefore let know all [the] house of Israel that both Lord him and Christ made the God, this the Jesus whom you crucified.

en.L: Therefore let all [the] house of Israel know assuredly that God has made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} both Lord and {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, this Jesus whom you crucified."
en.B: So let the whole house of Israel know for certain: God has made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} both Lord and {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, this Jesus whom you crucified."
en.R: So all the people of Israel should know this for sure: God has made Jesus both Lord and {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}. This is the same Jesus you nailed to a cross!"

decisions.choice: all the house of Israel: the whole people of Israel
decisions.reason: "House" means a family descended from one father, as in Luke 1:27, 1:33.

decisions.choice: God has made him Lord and Christ: God has openly set him in his place by raising and exalting him
alternatives: he became Lord and Christ only then
decisions.reason: Luke calls Jesus "Christ the Lord" at his birth (Luke 2:11). Peter speaks of what God has now done and shown: raised him and seated him at his right hand (2:32-35).

decisions.choice: Lord: the title of the one at God's right hand
decisions.reason: "Lord" ties together the Lord on whom people call (2:21) and David's Lord (2:34).

decisions.choice: whom you crucified: the last words, for emphasis
decisions.reason: Peter ends on the hearers' part in his death, which moves them in 2:37.

decisions.choice: Christ, with "Messiah" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As everywhere.

source.text: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ κατενύγησαν τὴν καρδίαν, εἶπόν τε πρὸς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ τοὺς λοιποὺς ἀποστόλους· Τί ποιήσωμεν, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί;

records.literal_gloss: Having heard then they were pierced the heart, said and to the Peter and the rest apostles, What shall we do, men brothers?

en.L: And having heard [this], they were pierced to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, "What shall we do, men, brothers?"
en.B: These words pierced their hearts. They asked Peter and the rest of the apostles, "What are we to do, brothers?"
en.R: The people were deeply troubled by what Peter said. They asked him and the other apostles, "Brothers, what must we do?"

decisions.choice: pierced to the heart: stung with sorrow and guilt
decisions.reason: The verb means to stab or prick. They know they have done wrong.

decisions.choice: men, brothers: here said to the apostles, who are men
decisions.reason: The crowd answers Peter with his own address (2:29), speaking to Peter and the other apostles.

decisions.choice: brothers, with no setting
decisions.reason: The apostles are men, so there is no inclusive form.

source.text: Πέτρος δὲ πρὸς αὐτούς· Μετανοήσατε, καὶ βαπτισθήτω ἕκαστος ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς ἄφεσιν τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ὑμῶν, καὶ λήμψεσθε τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος·

records.literal_gloss: Peter then to them, Repent and let be baptized each of you in the name of Jesus Christ for forgiveness of the sins of you, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

en.L: And Peter [said] to them, "Repent, and let each of you be baptized in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} for [the] forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
en.B: Peter answered them, "Repent, and every one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, so that your sins may be forgiven; and you will receive the Holy Spirit as a gift.
en.R: Peter told them, "Turn away from your sins and come back to God. Each one of you must be baptized in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, so that God will forgive your sins. And you will receive the Holy Spirit as a gift from God.

decisions.choice: repent: change one's mind and life, turning back to God
decisions.reason: As in John the Baptist's message (Luke 3:3, 3:8). They are to change their mind about Jesus and their whole way.

decisions.choice: in the name of Jesus Christ: calling on him, and coming under him
decisions.reason: Those who call on the Lord's name will be saved (2:21); in baptism they call on Jesus and are marked as his (22:16).

decisions.choice: for the forgiveness of your sins: so that sins are forgiven, as the goal of repenting and being baptized
decisions.reason: The word "for" here points to a goal, as in Luke 3:3. It goes with both commands, repenting and being baptized; in 3:19 forgiveness follows repentance with no word about baptism.

decisions.choice: the gift of the Holy Spirit: the gift that is the Spirit himself
decisions.reason: In 10:45 and 11:17 the gift is the Spirit poured out.

decisions.choice: turn away from your sins and come back to God
decisions.reason: Readable says what repenting means, as at Matthew 3:2.

decisions.choice: receive the Holy Spirit as a gift
alternatives: receive the gift of the Holy Spirit
decisions.reason: This wording shows that the gift is the Spirit.

source.text: ὑμῖν γάρ ἐστιν ἡ ἐπαγγελία καὶ τοῖς τέκνοις ὑμῶν καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς εἰς μακρὰν ὅσους ἂν προσκαλέσηται κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: To you for is the promise and to the children of you and to all those at far, as many as if will call to [himself] Lord the God of us.

en.L: For the promise is to you and to your children and to all those who are far off, as many as [the] Lord our God will call to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}."
en.B: The promise belongs to you and your children, and to all who are far away, everyone whom the Lord our God calls to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}."
en.R: God made this promise to you and to your children. It is also for people who live far away. It is for everyone the Lord our God calls to come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: the promise: the Spirit, promised by the Father (1:4, 2:33)
decisions.reason: The word looks back to 2:33, "the promise of the Holy Spirit".

decisions.choice: those far off: people far from Israel, the Gentiles
decisions.reason: Isaiah 57:19 speaks of peace to the far and the near, and Ephesians 2:13-17 applies it to the Gentiles. Peter may mean only Jews in distant lands; Acts 10-11 shows the promise reaching Gentiles.

decisions.choice: whom the Lord our God will call: the end of Joel 2:32
decisions.reason: Joel 2:32 ends "among the survivors whom the LORD calls". Peter finishes the verse he began in 2:21.

source.text: ἑτέροις τε λόγοις πλείοσιν διεμαρτύρατο, καὶ παρεκάλει αὐτοὺς λέγων· Σώθητε ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς τῆς σκολιᾶς ταύτης.

records.literal_gloss: Other and words many he testified and was urging them, saying, Be saved from the generation the crooked this.

en.L: And with many other words he testified and was urging them, saying, "Be saved from this crooked generation."
en.B: He went on to bear witness with many more words and kept appealing to them: "Let yourselves be rescued from this crooked generation!"
en.R: Peter said many other things to warn them. He kept begging them, "Let God save you from the evil people of this time!"

decisions.choice: be saved: let yourselves be saved, by God
alternatives: save yourselves by your own effort
decisions.reason: The verb is passive. God is the one who saves (2:21, 2:47), and they are to let it happen by turning to him.

decisions.choice: this crooked generation: the words of Deuteronomy 32:5
decisions.reason: Moses calls Israel "a crooked and twisted generation" (Deuteronomy 32:5; also Psalm 78:8). Peter means the people of his day who rejected Jesus.

decisions.choice: testified: spoke with solemn warning
decisions.reason: The word means to bear witness earnestly, often as a warning (20:21).

decisions.choice: let God save you
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: οἱ μὲν οὖν ἀποδεξάμενοι τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ ἐβαπτίσθησαν, καὶ προσετέθησαν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ψυχαὶ ὡσεὶ τρισχίλιαι.

records.literal_gloss: Those indeed therefore having received the word of him were baptized, and were added in the day that souls about three thousand.

en.L: So those who received his word were baptized, and there were added on that day about 3,000 souls.
en.B: Then those who welcomed what he said were baptized; that day about 3,000 people joined them.
en.R: Many people accepted what Peter said and were baptized. About 3,000 people joined the group of believers that day.

decisions.choice: souls: persons
decisions.reason: "Souls" is a way of counting people, as in Genesis 46:27 and Acts 27:37.

decisions.choice: were added: God added them
alternatives: they joined by their own choice
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the one who adds unnamed; 2:47 names him: the Lord.

decisions.choice: joined them (B); joined the group of believers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what they were added to, as 2:47 does.

source.text: ἦσαν δὲ προσκαρτεροῦντες τῇ διδαχῇ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ τῇ κοινωνίᾳ, τῇ κλάσει τοῦ ἄρτου καὶ ταῖς προσευχαῖς.

records.literal_gloss: They were then continuing in the teaching of the apostles and in the fellowship, in the breaking of the bread and in the prayers.

en.L: And they were devoting themselves to the teaching of the apostles and to the fellowship, to the breaking of the bread and to the prayers.
en.B: They gave themselves fully to the apostles' teaching and to the shared life, to the breaking of bread and to the prayers.
en.R: The believers kept learning from what the apostles taught. They shared their lives with one another. They shared meals together, and they prayed together.

decisions.choice: fellowship: sharing a common life
decisions.reason: The word means a sharing or partnership. 2:44-45 shows what it meant: they shared what they had.

decisions.choice: the breaking of bread: shared meals, likely including the Lord's Supper
decisions.reason: Jesus broke bread at the last supper (Luke 22:19) and at Emmaus (Luke 24:30, 24:35). In 20:7 believers meet "to break bread". In 2:46 the meals are eaten at home with gladness.

decisions.choice: the prayers: prayer together, perhaps the set prayers
decisions.reason: The article may point to the set hours of Jewish prayer, which they still kept (3:1).

decisions.choice: four things, in two pairs
decisions.reason: The Greek joins teaching with fellowship, and breaking of bread with prayers.

decisions.choice: shared meals together
decisions.reason: Readable keeps to what is certain: they ate together. The meaning note explains the rest.

source.text: Ἐγίνετο δὲ πάσῃ ψυχῇ φόβος, πολλά τε τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα διὰ τῶν ἀποστόλων ἐγίνετο.

records.literal_gloss: Was coming then upon every soul fear, many and wonders and signs through the apostles were happening.

en.L: And fear was coming upon every soul, and many wonders and signs were happening through the apostles.
en.B: Everyone felt a deep awe, and many wonders and signs took place through the apostles.
en.R: Everyone was filled with deep respect for God, because God did many wonders and signs through the apostles.

decisions.choice: fear: awe before God's power
decisions.reason: The fear that comes when God is plainly at work, as in Luke 5:26, 7:16.

decisions.choice: every soul: everyone, believers and those outside
decisions.reason: In 5:11 the fear comes on the church and all who heard.

decisions.choice: through the apostles: God worked the signs through them
decisions.reason: As God did signs through Jesus (2:22); Peter says so in 3:12-16.

decisions.choice: respect for God; because God did
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they feared and who did the signs, as the meaning notes explain.

source.text: πάντες δὲ οἱ πιστεύοντες ἦσαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ καὶ εἶχον ἅπαντα κοινά, καὶ τὰ κτήματα καὶ τὰς ὑπάρξεις ἐπίπρασκον καὶ διεμέριζον αὐτὰ πᾶσιν καθότι ἄν τις χρείαν εἶχεν·

records.literal_gloss: All then the believing were together and had all things common, \v 45 and the properties and the possessions they were selling and were distributing them to all, as anyone need had.

en.L: And all who believed were together and had all things in common, \v 45 and they were selling [their] properties and possessions and distributing them to all, as anyone had need.
en.B: Everyone who believed kept together and treated all they had as shared. \v 45 They would sell off land and goods and divide the money among all, according to what each one needed.
en.R: All the believers stayed together and shared everything they had. \v 45 They sold their land and the things they owned. Then they gave the money to anyone who needed it.

decisions.choice: were selling and distributing: they did this again and again, as needs arose
alternatives: they all sold everything at once
decisions.reason: The tenses describe repeated actions. 4:34-37 and 5:4 show that people sold what they chose, when there was need.

decisions.choice: properties and possessions: land, and other belongings
alternatives: two words for the same thing
decisions.reason: The first word usually means land or fields (5:1), the second goods of any kind.

decisions.choice: together: in one place, or in one mind
decisions.reason: The same phrase as 1:15 and 2:1. It may mean they met in one place, or that they were united.

decisions.choice: the money
decisions.reason: What they shared out was the money from the sales.

source.text: καθ’ ἡμέραν τε προσκαρτεροῦντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, κλῶντές τε κατ’ οἶκον ἄρτον, μετελάμβανον τροφῆς ἐν ἀγαλλιάσει καὶ ἀφελότητι καρδίας, αἰνοῦντες τὸν θεὸν καὶ ἔχοντες χάριν πρὸς ὅλον τὸν λαόν.

records.literal_gloss: Daily and continuing with one mind in the temple, breaking and house by house bread, they were sharing food with gladness and simplicity of heart, \v 47 praising the God and having favor with all the people.

en.L: And day by day, continuing with one mind in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, they were sharing food with gladness and simplicity of heart, \v 47 praising God and having favor with all the people.
en.B: Day after day they went on gathering, united, in the temple; at home they broke bread, eating their food with joyful and simple hearts, \v 47 praising God and well regarded by all the people.
en.R: Every day the believers met together in the temple courtyard. They also ate meals together in their homes. They were glad, and their hearts were open and generous. \v 47 They praised God, and all the people liked them.

decisions.choice: the temple: the temple courts, where people gathered
decisions.reason: The word means the whole temple area. Solomon's Porch was one of its places to meet (3:11, 5:12).

decisions.choice: simplicity of heart: a heart without guile, open and generous
decisions.reason: The word means singleness, being undivided; Paul uses a related word for generous giving (Romans 12:8; 2 Corinthians 8:2).

decisions.choice: favor: the goodwill of the people toward them
alternatives: the believers showed kindness to the people
decisions.reason: The word usually rendered "grace" here means favor in people's eyes, as in Luke 2:52. The people thought well of them. Some read it the other way: the believers were kind to all.

decisions.choice: house by house: in their homes
decisions.reason: They met in one home and another, as well as in the temple.

decisions.choice: having favor (L); well regarded (B); liked them (R)
decisions.reason: This is the key term "grace", but here it means human favor, as the meaning note explains.

source.text: ὁ δὲ κύριος προσετίθει τοὺς σῳζομένους καθ’ ἡμέραν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό.

records.literal_gloss: The and Lord was adding those being saved daily together.

en.L: And the Lord was adding those who were being saved day by day together.
en.B: And each day the Lord brought into their company more people who were being saved.
en.R: Every day the Lord added more people to their group, people {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saving.

decisions.choice: those who were being saved: the people God was saving
decisions.reason: The tense describes saving still going on, as in 1 Corinthians 1:18.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "together", that is, to their number
decisions.reason: Some later manuscripts add "to the church" here; the King James Version follows them. The earliest manuscripts end with "together" and begin 3:1 with these words. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Lord: the risen Jesus, or God
decisions.reason: The Lord whom people call on (2:21, 2:36) adds them. The one who adds is not the apostles.

decisions.choice: into their company (B); to their group (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek phrase means "to the same", the group of believers.
